milestones.label: Groups of polynomial growth theorem
milestones.work: M. Gromov, Groups of polynomial growth and expanding maps, Publ. Math. IHES 53 (1981) 53-78
milestones.description: Proves that finitely generated groups of polynomial growth are virtually nilpotent, using large-scale geometry of the Cayley graph.

evidence.claim: Crossref record: Gromov, Publ. Math. IHES 53, 53-78, 1981

notes: Crossref confirmed the 1981 IHES paper. The 1987 'Hyperbolic groups' (MSRI Publ. 8) and the 1993 asymptotic-invariants work were not opened, so no first_statement, naming or institution milestone is recorded. Catalogue dates 1981/1987/1993 are unverified.

milestones.label: Non-commutative differential geometry
milestones.work: A. Connes, Non-commutative differential geometry, Publ. Math. IHES 62 (1985) 41-144
milestones.description: Develops cyclic cohomology and differential calculus on operator algebras as noncommutative spaces.

evidence.claim: Crossref record: Connes, Publ. Math. IHES 62, 41-144, 1985

notes: Crossref confirmed the 1985 IHES paper. The Springer LNM 'Introduction to non commutative differential geometry' candidate (doi 10.1007/bfb0084582) was not opened. The 1994 book and an earlier 1980 precursor were not verified, so no consolidation or naming milestone.

milestones.label: Freedman classifies simply connected topological 4-manifolds
milestones.work: M. H. Freedman, The topology of four-dimensional manifolds, J. Differential Geom. 17 (1982) 357-453
milestones.description: Classifies simply connected closed topological four-manifolds, the contrast case for Donaldson's smooth results.

milestones.label: Donaldson: gauge theory restricts smooth 4-manifolds
milestones.work: S. K. Donaldson, An application of gauge theory to four-dimensional topology, J. Differential Geom. 18 (1983) 279-315
milestones.description: Uses moduli of Yang-Mills instantons to show smooth definite 4-manifolds have diagonalizable intersection forms.

milestones.label: Donaldson announcement
milestones.work: S. K. Donaldson, Self-dual connections and the topology of smooth 4-manifolds, Bull. AMS 8 (1983) 81-83
milestones.description: Short announcement of the self-dual connection method.
milestones.note: Publication year of announcement equals the full paper; either may be treated as the public start.

notes: All three works confirmed in Crossref. Witten, Monopoles and four-manifolds (Math. Res. Lett. 1, 1994) was not verified (search rate-limited), so Seiberg-Witten stage is unrecorded.

milestones.label: Pseudo-holomorphic curves in symplectic manifolds
milestones.work: M. Gromov, Pseudo holomorphic curves in symplectic manifolds, Invent. Math. 82 (1985) 307-347
milestones.description: Introduces holomorphic curve methods giving non-squeezing and rigidity in symplectic geometry.

milestones.label: Floer: Morse theory for Lagrangian intersections
milestones.work: A. Floer, Morse theory for Lagrangian intersections, J. Differential Geom. 28 (1988) 513-547
milestones.description: Defines Floer homology to prove Arnold's Lagrangian intersection conjecture in cases.

notes: Crossref confirmed Gromov 1985 and Floer 1988. Arnold's Mathematical Methods of Classical Mechanics (Springer, 1978 English) was not opened. No first_statement or naming milestone established.

milestones.label: Conway-Norton Monstrous moonshine
milestones.work: J. H. Conway, S. P. Norton, Monstrous moonshine, Bull. London Math. Soc. 11 (1979) 308-339
milestones.description: Formulates the moonshine conjectures linking Monster conjugacy classes to Hauptmoduln.

evidence.claim: Crossref record: Conway and Norton, BLMS 11, 308-339, 1979

milestones.note: Name 'monstrous moonshine' appears in the title, so this also plays the naming role.

milestones.label: Borcherds proves the moonshine conjecture
milestones.work: R. E. Borcherds, Monstrous moonshine and monstrous Lie superalgebras, Invent. Math. 109 (1992) 405-444
milestones.description: Proves the Conway-Norton conjectures using the monster vertex algebra and a Lie superalgebra.

notes: Crossref confirmed both. Frenkel-Lepowsky-Meurman 1988 book not verified. Conway-Norton's 'naming' role not separately recorded; it is the same paper.

canonicalName: Modularity of elliptic curves and Fermat's Last Theorem

milestones.label: Ribet: epsilon conjecture
milestones.work: K. A. Ribet, On modular representations of Gal(Q-bar/Q) arising from modular forms, Invent. Math. 100 (1990) 431-476
milestones.description: Shows modularity of semistable curves would imply Fermat's Last Theorem (Frey curve link).

milestones.label: Wiles proves modularity of semistable elliptic curves
milestones.work: A. Wiles, Modular elliptic curves and Fermat's Last Theorem, Ann. of Math. 141 (1995)
milestones.description: Proves modularity for semistable curves, hence Fermat's Last Theorem.

evidence.claim: Crossref record: Wiles, Annals of Math. 141, 1995

notes: Crossref confirmed Ribet 1990 and Wiles 1995. Frey 1986 (Ann. Univ. Sarav.) and Taylor-Wiles 1995 not opened, so no first_statement. Springer chapter doi 10.1007/978-3-0348-9078-6_18 not opened.

canonicalName: Perelman's proof of the Poincare conjecture

milestones.label: Hamilton introduces Ricci flow
milestones.work: R. S. Hamilton, Three-manifolds with positive Ricci curvature, J. Differential Geom. 17 (1982) 255-306
milestones.description: Introduces Ricci flow and proves convergence to round metric for positive Ricci curvature three-manifolds.

milestones.label: Entropy formula for the Ricci flow
milestones.work: G. Perelman, The entropy formula for the Ricci flow and its geometric applications, arXiv:math/0211159 (2002)
milestones.description: Introduces the entropy functional and no-local-collapsing.

milestones.label: Ricci flow with surgery
milestones.work: G. Perelman, Ricci flow with surgery on three-manifolds, arXiv:math/0303109 (2003)
milestones.description: Constructs Ricci flow with surgery on three-manifolds.

milestones.label: Finite extinction time
milestones.work: G. Perelman, Finite extinction time for the solutions to the Ricci flow on certain three-manifolds, arXiv:math/0307245 (2003)
milestones.description: Shows extinction in finite time, completing the route to Poincare.

notes: Hamilton 1982 identified via Crossref (inherited year correct); three arXiv records opened via the arXiv API. Verification papers (Kleiner-Lott, Cao-Zhu, Morgan-Tian) and recognition (Clay prize) were not searched.

milestones.label: Matomaki-Radziwill short intervals
milestones.work: K. Matomaki, M. Radziwill, Multiplicative functions in short intervals, Ann. of Math. 183 (2016) 1015-1056
milestones.description: Short-interval results for multiplicative functions used in the Tao solution.
milestones.note: Relevance to the problem is from the inherited catalogue, not from reading the paper.

milestones.label: Tao: logarithmically averaged Chowla/Elliott
milestones.work: T. Tao, The logarithmically averaged Chowla and Elliott conjectures for two-point correlations, Forum Math. Pi 4 (2016)
milestones.description: Proves the two-point log-averaged Elliott result underlying the discrepancy solution.

milestones.label: Tao: The Erdos discrepancy problem
milestones.work: T. Tao, The Erdos discrepancy problem, Discrete Analysis 2016
milestones.description: Resolves the Erdos discrepancy problem.

notes: Crossref confirmed all three (2016 journal years; preprints were earlier, 2015, not checked). Erdos 1932 conjecture, Polymath5 and Konev-Lisitsa not searched, so no first_statement.

milestones.label: Knuth: Computer science and its relation to mathematics
milestones.work: D. E. Knuth, Computer Science and its Relation to Mathematics, Amer. Math. Monthly 81 (1974) 323-343
milestones.description: Essay discussing computer science as a discipline distinct from mathematics.
milestones.note: Reflective essay, not a founding event; role chosen cautiously.

notes: Only Knuth's 1974 essay was verified (Crossref). Turing 1936 and department/journal institutions (e.g. Purdue 1962, ACM) not verified; no institution milestone.

canonicalName: Complex analysis and the primes: Riemann's zeta function to the prime number theorem

milestones.label: Hadamard's prime number theorem proof
milestones.work: J. Hadamard, Sur la distribution des zeros de la fonction zeta(s) et ses consequences arithmetiques, Bull. Soc. Math. France 24 (1896) 199-220
milestones.description: Proves zeta has no zeros on Re s = 1 and deduces the prime number theorem.

notes: Crossref confirmed Hadamard 1896 (its metadata lists volume 2 erroneously; 24 is the inherited value, unchecked). Riemann 1859 and de la Vallee Poussin 1896 not opened, so no first_statement.

milestones.label: Grothendieck: Sur quelques points d'algebre homologique
milestones.work: A. Grothendieck, Sur quelques points d'algebre homologique, I, Tohoku Math. J. (2) 9 (1957)
milestones.description: Develops abelian categories and derived functors for sheaves.

notes: Crossref confirmed part I (1957); part II candidate not opened. Cartan-Eilenberg 1956 book not verified in a bibliographic record (search rate-limited), so no consolidation milestone.

canonicalName: K-theory and Grothendieck-Riemann-Roch: algebraic geometry enters topology

milestones.label: Borel-Serre: Le theoreme de Riemann-Roch
milestones.work: A. Borel, J.-P. Serre, Le theoreme de Riemann-Roch, Bull. Soc. Math. France 86 (1958) 97-136
milestones.description: Publishes Grothendieck's Riemann-Roch theorem with proof.

evidence.claim: Crossref record: Borel and Serre, pp. 97-136, 1958

milestones.note: Crossref lists volume 79; the 1958 year is consistent with volume 86.

milestones.label: Atiyah-Hirzebruch: Vector bundles and homogeneous spaces
milestones.work: M. F. Atiyah, F. Hirzebruch, Vector bundles and homogeneous spaces, Proc. Sympos. Pure Math. 3 (1961) 7-38
milestones.description: Introduces topological K-theory.

evidence.claim: Crossref record: Proc. Sympos. Pure Math. 3, 7-38, 1961

notes: Crossref confirmed both. Hirzebruch 1956 book (Springer dois not opened) and Atiyah's K-theory 1967 not verified; no first_statement.
